content.text: The rule is satisfied at the fallback level. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 (continuing at p0090-p0093) contains a Garman-given IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns or controls all rights necessary and indemnifies Sparkling against Losses (including settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees) arising from breach of that non-infringement/title warranty, backed by the customary remedy ladder of procure the right, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify (p0091-p0093). No exclusions for our modifications, combinations or specifications are imposed, and there is no super-cap — indeed Section 15 expressly disapplies the liability limitation to breaches of Section 13, so the indemnity is uncapped, which is better than the 3x fallback and benefits us. Critically, there is no customer-side indemnity anywhere in the agreement (searches for "indemnif", "harmless" and "defend" return only p0090), so the walk-away scenarios (no vendor IP indemnity, or a one-way customer indemnity) do not arise. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback position and is not redlined. Noted for the file only, short of the preferred position and not flagged as deviations: the indemnity is "indemnify and hold harmless" without an express duty to defend or allocation of defence/settlement control and cooperation mechanics; there is no refund remedy if none of (a)-(c) can be achieved; the ten calendar day notice window is tight; and the indemnity is limited to IP/title matters, without separate prongs for Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to Sparkling data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. These are sub-elements of the preferred position and can be raised commercially if the negotiation reopens Section 13.
